No. 16-2, effective 2016-05-17 -- subsequent amendments (e.g. DPA2026-00006) may have updated specific by-right/SUP boundaries since; confirm current text at the Municode link before relying on specific section numbers.
jurisdiction.pilot_notes: Zoning geometry live-verified 2026-08-13 (gisweb.pwcva.gov Planning/Zoning/MapServer layer 5 'Zoning Districts', 2,227 features, field ZoningDistrict). Data-center permitted-use research completed 2026-08-15 for 28 of 31 real district codes against real, primary-source PWC ordinance text: PWC's own 'Data Center Overlay Frequently Asked Questions' PDF and the verbatim 2016 ordinance amendment text (Ord. No. 16-2, Sec. 32-403.33 and Sec. 32-509.01-.06), both fetched and text-extracted directly from the government PDFs via a GitHub-Actions-dispatched pdf-parse run -- not a search-engine summary. 17 districts are prohibited (agricultural, residential, PMR, B-2, B-3, V), 11 are Special-Use-Permit-eligible outside the Data Center Opportunity Zone Overlay District (with several of those -- O(F)/O(H)/O(L)/O(M)/M-1/M-2/M-T -- upgrading to by-right when the parcel is also inside the overlay). CTY, FED, and TWN remain genuinely unresearched. The Overlay District's real boundary geometry (Planning/Zoning/MapServer layer 7 'Overlay District Data Center Opportunity Zone') has been found but is not yet wired into the pipeline as a queryable overlay -- so today's classification always uses the base-district (outside-overlay) permission level, never the more permissive by-right-in-overlay level, which is the conservative/honest direction to be wrong in.
known_limitations: The Data Center Opportunity Zone Overlay District's real GIS boundary (layer 7) is not yet wired into the pipeline as a queryable overlay -- every classification currently reflects the base district's outside-overlay permission level (Special Use Permit for most non-prohibited districts), even for parcels that may actually be inside the overlay and therefore eligible by-right under Sec. 32-509.03. This is the conservative direction to be wrong in (understates eligibility, never overstates it), but it is a known gap, not a determination that overlay membership doesn't matter.
CTY, FED, and TWN district codes could not be matched to an official category via primary-source research after multiple targeted searches -- they remain 'not_listed', not a claim of prohibition.

District official names are only recorded where directly confirmed via a primary or clearly-attributed secondary source (SR-1/SR-1C/SR-5 'Semi-Rural Residential', RPC 'Residential Planned Community', MXD-U 'Mixed Use District-Urban'); most other codes' exact official titles are still unconfirmed even though their category and DC-eligibility are.
The Planning/Zoning/MapServer layer 5 'Zoning Districts' has no separate district-name field -- ZoningDistrict is the only classification attribute from the source itself.
Dimensional standards (setbacks, height, lot coverage) have not been researched for any district -- no buildable-envelope estimate is possible yet for Prince William parcels.
jurisdiction.notes: Second Virginia pilot jurisdiction after Loudoun. Geometry pipeline proven end-to-end; 28 of 31 real district codes now carry ordinance-text-verified data-center permitted-use determinations. Remaining gaps: 3 unresearched codes (CTY/FED/TWN), the overlay boundary not yet wired spatially, and no dimensional standards yet.

DCOZOD.overlay_name: Data Center Opportunity Zone Overlay District
DCOZOD.description: Adopted in 2016 (Ord. No. 16-2) to promote data center development in areas of the county with existing infrastructure capable of supporting the use, while continuing to attract high-tech industrial development and limiting negative impacts to surrounding communities. The Overlay does not replace the underlying base zoning district -- both the underlying district's regulations and the Overlay's own regulations apply together. The Overlay covers approximately 9,500 acres; per PWC's own FAQ, roughly 72% of all industrially-zoned land countywide falls within it.
DCOZOD.geographic_coverage: Approximately 9,500 acres, concentrated in the county's existing office/industrial corridor. Real boundary geometry exists as a GIS layer (gisweb.pwcva.gov, Planning/Zoning/MapServer layer 7, 'Overlay District Data Center Opportunity Zone') but has not yet been fetched/wired into this pipeline as a queryable spatial layer -- see known_geometry_gap.
